# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — create capability from empty seed: values-not-formulas contract + openpyxl edit-in-place + inspect/verify/DONE procedure
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md (new, was empty): role line; "How your file is graded" (data_only, no recalc → literal typed values even when a formula/VBA is requested; keep layout) [cluster A];
  - openpyxl edit-in-place by explicit coordinate, sheet by name, save via openpyxl not to_excel [B];
  - inspect real cells + treat in-sheet examples/expected blocks as spec [C];
  - dual load for cached values + error inputs treated as missing [D];
  - verify by data_only reload + plain-text DONE [E];
  - one generic `<example>` skeleton.
  - task_template.md (new): same 6 fields + {max_turns}; preview index ≠ Excel row; Sheet-Level compared at exact coordinates; closing block replaces "once that file exists, you are done" with Inspect→Solve→Verify→DONE.
- Expected effect + safety:
  - A should flip the 7 recalc-correct formula tasks (37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942) and possibly 56563/54144/37456.
  - B/C target 50768, 227-40, 48527, 39046, 43436, 59196, 51-12. D targets 267-18.
  - Safe: no passing trace writes a formula, and to_excel passes (9726, 382-10, 12864, 142-12, 2768) are plain row-1-header tables where an openpyxl write at the same coordinates is equivalent.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (first iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 80-42 (95k-cell consolidation), 9569 (1280-cell range left empty), the semantic-misread tail.
- Plateau signal: n/a.
- Focus next iteration:
  - Read this RESULT's broke/fixed. If a to_excel-passing task broke, soften the openpyxl-save line to "when the sheet has non-table layout / multiple sheets".
  - Then examine residual failing traces for semantic misreads.
  - Check whether the agent now ends with DONE, or still loops.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.800 Δ=+0.350 · fixed={37378, 37456, 39046, 46897, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 6698, 7902, 80-42, 8942, 9569} · broke={402-43, 45635} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.800 Δ=+0.350 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — reconcile-with-examples procedure + round-1 dump script + label/axis mapping + table-shape and formula-cell contracts
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md: graded rule 2 says no formula may remain in answer_position; untouched formulas become their cached value [J, 267-18].
  - "## Rounds" says only the first python block runs [L].
  - Workflow 1 is a fixed round-1 dump script printing every non-empty cell with cached value and formula, capped in size [H].
  - Workflow 2 is an ordered a/b/c: list examples (placeholders are not examples) → labels on both axes + same-label mapping + comparison set follows what is shared → reconcile computed vs existing and change the rule until all match [F, G: 48527, 51-12, 43436, 50768, 45635].
  - Float-threshold tolerance [K, 51-12].
  - Workflow 4 table contract: source ends at the first blank row; a new sheet starts with the header; copy the example shape with blanks in place [I: 402-43, 227-40].
  - The example handles untouched formula cells.
  - task_template.md: closing steps become Inspect (dump) → Specify → Solve (+reconcile, +formula→value) → Verify → DONE; only the first block executes.
- Expected effect + safety:
  - Targets all 8 failures, including the 2 cand_0001 broke (402-43, 45635).
  - Passing tasks with pre-fills (9569, 12864, 48921) are gold-consistent, and 59595's 'n/a' placeholders are excluded from "examples".
  - Formula-in-answer passing tasks already overwrite every such cell.
  - The dump script is read-only and tested on all 40 init files.
- Building on prior RESULTS: keeps all of cand_0001 (+0.350). Recovers 402-43 by an explicit header rule rather than reverting the to_excel guidance.
- Refuted hypotheses: none (rejected.jsonl empty).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: the semantic misreads where examples are absent; the prompt now relies on gemma actually running the reconcile print.
- Plateau signal: n/a (one accept so far).
- Focus next iteration:
  - If val drops, the most likely culprits are the longer prompt or the reconcile step on a passing task. Check which passing tasks broke and whether their traces mention "examples"/"mismatch".
  - Prune the specific sub-rule involved, not the whole procedure.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.825 Δ=+0.025 · fixed={267-18, 402-43, 45635, 48527, 50768} · broke={31628, 37456, 560-12, 80-42} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0002: ACCEPTED val=0.825 Δ=+0.025 -->

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0003 — placement/append contract + source-extent and empty-range rules + direct-reading/header rule + printed per-cell reconcile + DONE trigger
- Changes I made (prompt.md unless noted):
  - Workflow 4 gets a "Placement" bullet: the instruction's start cell wins over answer_position's top-left [560-12]. It also gets an "Appending" bullet: first available rows / append means keep existing rows and write after the last one; never clear [80-42]. Template step 2 asks for both.
  - Workflow 3: next/previous/last-row rules read the whole source column, beyond answer_position [37456].
  - New 2d: if a named range is empty, use the populated range the examples describe [51-12].
  - New 2e: direct reading when no example contradicts it, and no flipping a verified answer without new evidence [31628]. A 2b sentence says header wording ("by end of <month>", "as of") sets the reference point [43436].
  - 2c plus template step 3: run the rule on the example block's own source rows and print coordinate/computed/expected/ok per cell, blanks included [227-40].
  - 2a: cached values of formulas being fixed are not examples (safety for 6698, 48620).
  - Prompt step 6 and template step 5: a verify output identical to the previous round's means DONE [53647 loop].
- Expected effect + safety:
  - Targets all 7 failures, including all 4 that cand_0002 broke (31628, 37456, 560-12, 80-42). The goal is to recover them without reverting cand_0002's gains.
  - Trigger phrases were grepped across the 40 val instructions. "add to the bottom" was dropped because 402-43 and 50768 use "bottom" in another sense. Every passing named-cell instruction names answer_position's top-left.
- Building on prior RESULTS: keeps all of cand_0001 and cand_0002. For each task cand_0002 broke, I read the cand_0001 trace that passed, and the new rule encodes what that trace did.
- Refuted hypotheses: none (no rejects).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: none known beyond these 7. The remaining risk is that gemma ignores the printed reconcile (a behavioral gap).
- Focus next iteration (if any): check whether the per-cell `ok` print actually appears in traces. If val drops, look first at the Placement and Appending triggers, then at the 2e "no flip" clause.
